items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: You never heard of Nene Bryant even had him. He was a drummer, a good one.

ctx.x: S-T-O-R-O-D-E. Conant? Yeah, Trum. He was good too. Yeah, a lot of fellows used to have him. You never heard of Nene Bryant even had him. He was a drummer, a good one. He played with Tick Chambers at Miss Cole Lawnbottom. And there was a kid around there, he died young, Jim Williams. And he used to, we couldn't go in the pool room, but he had long parents on, he had long parents. He was considered a man. And he sat on the pool room table and played for us. Now later on they said he was going to be one of the…
And he wrote a lot of tunes too, you know.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: So there was Nene Bryant, the drummer, and James Williams...

ctx.x: Yeah, I know he teaches all that.

And I saw Roy a little later in the arms playing the baritone, I think in the Arnold band. So these things just begin to, you'll have to pardon me because it just began to come to me. That was Sammy Stewart's band was at the old Sunset. You said Stewart. Now that's come to me now. And so we were renting from some people to call their liveazos. And the B-sants was right across the street. They were becoming great ball players, champion B-sants. So I'll go on back to the music now. So there was Nene Bryant, the…
Excuse me for interrupting you again, but about your home and all, did your mother ever sing? Or did anyone? I'm sorry. Well yes, my mother. You don't have to keep those in, it'll pick up anything.
